notice: All organisations, people, events and statistics in this file are fictional. These are evidence-reasoning regression cases, not a real-world accuracy benchmark.

cases.claim: Port Ember Council indirectly owns a majority of Larkline Ferries.
cases.reason: Two contemporaneous ownership links establish 100% ownership of a holding company and its 70% holding in the ferry company. They do not establish day-to-day management.

sources.title: Port Ember holdings register
sources.passage: As at 1 October 2026, Port Ember Council owns 100% of the ordinary shares and voting rights in Harbourlight Holdings. Harbourlight Holdings is a separate corporate entity.

sources.title: Larkline Ferries share register
sources.passage: As at 1 October 2026, Harbourlight Holdings owns 70% of the ordinary shares and voting rights in Larkline Ferries. All remaining shares are widely held. No special voting arrangements alter those percentages.

cases.claim: Port Ember Council directly manages Larkline Ferries' daily operations.
cases.reason: The explicit operational statement contradicts direct council management, despite its indirect ownership.

sources.title: Larkline Ferries governance statement
sources.passage: Port Ember Council indirectly owns 70% of Larkline Ferries through Harbourlight Holdings. The council does not directly manage the company's daily operations. Larkline Ferries' independent board and executive management make all daily operating decisions.

cases.claim: Alder City's household recycling participation rate doubled between 2024 and 2025.
cases.reason: Participating household count doubled, but the proportion stayed at 50%; counts cannot substitute for rates.

sources.title: Alder City annual recycling participation
sources.passage: Alder City's annual household recycling participation rate is participating households divided by all eligible households. In 2024 there were 1,000 participating households out of 2,000 eligible households: a participation rate of 50%. In 2025 there were 2,000 participating households out of 4,000 eligible households: a participation rate of 50%. The rate therefore remained unchanged from 2024 to 2025, although the count doubled.

cases.claim: Meadowport's rental vacancy rate fell by half between 2025 and 2026.
cases.reason: The bulletin is published in 2026 but reports only 2022-2023. It cannot establish the claim's later period.

sources.title: Meadowport historical housing bulletin
sources.passage: Published 15 October 2026. Historical statistics reproduced without revision: Meadowport rental vacancy rate was 8% in 2022 and 4% in 2023. These figures describe 2022 and 2023, not 2025 or 2026. This bulletin contains no vacancy observations for 2025 or 2026.

cases.claim: Fenwick Council is not closing Willow Library on 1 December 2026.
cases.reason: Preserving 'not' is essential: the official announcement explicitly keeps this library open on the stated date.

sources.title: Willow Library opening arrangements
sources.passage: Fenwick Council confirms that Willow Library will remain open throughout 1 December 2026 under its normal opening hours. Willow Library is not closing on that date. A renovation at the separate Cedar Reading Room does not affect Willow Library.

cases.claim: Chief engineer Mira Sol said that River Arc Bridge is unsafe.
cases.reason: An inspection's safety conclusion does not establish what the named engineer said. No speech, quotation or denial is supplied.

sources.title: River Arc Bridge inspection summary
sources.passage: The October 2026 independent inspection found River Arc Bridge safe for normal traffic. The inspection report contains engineering measurements and the panel's conclusion. It does not report any statement made by chief engineer Mira Sol.

cases.claim: Bellhaven officials are privately discussing raising the residential waste levy to $900 next year.
cases.reason: The published existing rate cannot refute an alleged private discussion about a future change.

sources.title: Bellhaven current waste levy
sources.passage: Bellhaven's residential waste levy is $300 per household for the 2026 calendar year. This page lists the rule currently in force. It does not describe private discussions, draft proposals, or rates for 2027.

cases.claim: Hillford Transport Board announced free tram rides every Sunday starting 1 December 2026.
cases.reason: A dated official announcement explicitly confirms the announced change; the older fare policy must not override it.

sources.title: Hillford tram fare policy before the change
sources.passage: Until 30 November 2026, Hillford trams charge the normal fare every day, including Sundays.

sources.title: Hillford Sunday free travel announcement
sources.passage: On 2 November 2026, Hillford Transport Board announced that tram rides on every Hillford route will be free each Sunday from 1 December 2026 onward. Normal fares continue on other days. This announced scheme replaces the previous Sunday fare rule from its start date.

cases.claim: Baymere Reservoir is completely empty because illegal pipes have drained it.
cases.reason: A current 85% reading refutes the material 'completely empty' premise. The supplied evidence does not establish whether illegal pipes exist; that must remain unresolved.

sources.title: Baymere Reservoir current measurement
sources.passage: Baymere Water Authority measured Baymere Reservoir at 85% of usable storage capacity at 09:00 on 3 November 2026. The reservoir is not empty and continues normal supply. This level report contains no findings about illegal pipe connections or their effects.

cases.reason: A warning about exhausting one person's withdrawals is not a statement about the collective fund's assets, liabilities or solvency.

sources.title: Oakbridge Pension Fund member withdrawal guide
sources.passage: An individual member's personal retirement balance can run out if that member withdraws all their savings early. This warning concerns the member's own balance, not the financial position of Oakbridge Pension Fund. The guide supplies no audited assets, liabilities or solvency assessment for the fund.

cases.claim: All flights from Seabrook Airfield will be cancelled tomorrow.
cases.reason: An older routine operating schedule and lack of a cancellation announcement in the supplied pack do not establish tomorrow's actual flight status. No completed live announcement search or current operating bulletin is supplied.

sources.title: Seabrook Airfield routine hours
sources.passage: Seabrook Airfield's routine published operating hours are 06:00 to 22:00 daily. This general schedule was last updated on 1 June 2026 and does not provide day-specific flight status, disruption notices or cancellations for November 2026.
